text.p: Portugal Telecom and Spain's Telefonica have reached an agreement which will include the exchange of shares, a spokeswoman for the Portuguese company said on Tuesday.

She declined to confirm whether Telefonica would be taking the 3.0-3.5 percent stake in Portugal Telecom, with Telecom taking one percent of the Spanish group, reported by Spanish newspapers. But she said an exchange of shares was included.
"PT confirms an accord with Telefonica with a share exchange," she said.
But she added that the scope of the deal ranged well beyond a share swap. "The agreement (with Telefonica) is going to be wider than a simple exchange of shares," she said without giving details.
She said that the agreement would be signed on Wednesday after which details of the deal would be given at a news conference.
Telefonica chairman Juan Villalonga is due in Lisbon on either Wednesday or Thursday.
The accord with Telefonica followed an announcement on Monday that Portugal Telecom had opted for the Anglo-American venture Concert as its global ally.
Concert is made up of British Telecom and MCI which will both be taking small stakes in the Portuguese firm.
Telefonica is allied to Concert's biggest rival, the AT&T -led Unisource, but there has been speculation that it is about to jump ship.
